parsed.explanation: Combined regime: federal passport sex-marker restrictions are in force (Nov 2025), and an entry cable allows refusal on document discrepancy, with a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility finding. Documented federal custody harms include immigration-custody abuse of trans men and a corrections policy of conversion-style treatment from 2026. Division layer: gender identity was removed from state civil-rights law and local protections were preempted (2026), so there is no state remedy for service, housing or employment refusal. A school-ground birth-certificate restroom rule binds visitors. Willful entry plus refusal to depart is criminal trespass, with a documented 2025 handcuffed arrest and a 24-hour men's-ward hold. Under-18 care is banned. Interaction: a document discrepancy at entry or a facility incident can move a traveller into birth-sex custody. No capital exposure is documented. State violence data is absent and undercount floors are not used. Rated in the lower-elevated band, near birth-sex housing jurisdictions.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport sex markers restricted to M/F by birth-sex supporting documents; X markers no longer issued; passports confiscated or blocked, leaving travellers stranded. Entry cable directs refusal on any record discrepancy and allows a possible permanent fraud ineligibility finding.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid to expiry. Civil-liberties suit pending; policy challenged but in effect.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-passport mismatch at a US-issued document check or visa application can escalate to refusal, requests for evidence, or fraud allegation, which then leads into detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Division trespass offence for willful entry into opposite-sex restroom plus refusal to depart; 2025 arrest handcuffed and held 24 hours in men's ward. Immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men. Federal corrections adopted conversion-style policies from 2026 and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Pretrial release available; the division trespass offence requires refusal after an employee request, so automatic arrest on entry is not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility use in a public building can convert to criminal trespass, then to birth-sex placement; federal custody rules apply in the same chain.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal government-funded single-sex facilities barred for trans people; division school-ground rule binds all persons including visitors to birth-certificate restrooms and changing areas; state public-building trespass offence applies.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Single-person facility allowed for students only, conditional on written guardian consent. Adult restroom restriction outside school grounds not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rule and division school rule stack; the restroom rule is universal exposure on school campuses for adult visitors.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care under 18 (2023). Federal subpoenas for under-19 hospital records (summer 2025). Proposed federal rule to bar public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care (Oct 2025). Federal immigration and corrections care denial documented.
care_services.protection: Adult surgery coverage kept via 2019 ruling; that ruling is dated and its current operation is not documented.
care_services.interaction: Minor's care can be denied at home and records can be pulled federally; a visiting adult seeking care for a minor faces disclosure exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal EO directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition, partly enjoined. Dec 2025 and May 2026 federal counterterrorism documents name a 'radically pro-transgender' group as a priority; a cash-reward system was ordered. Official rhetoric is state-directed threat framing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism statement says powers will not target people who simply disagree; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing at federal level can affect visitors engaged in advocacy or school contact; the enjoinder status is uncertain.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor traveller cannot obtain gender-affirming care under 18 in the division. School-ground restroom rule binds an accompanying parent. Single-person student facility requires written guardian consent, which forces disclosure. Teacher prosecution EO risks school staff contact with minors.
minors_guardians.protection: Single-person facility is available to students with consent; enjoined portions of federal EOs may limit school enforcement.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's school visit can create guardian investigation and a documented-consent trail; care denial can separate a travelling child from needed treatment.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific homicide or violence figures; monitoring data are undercount floors and are not used. Police-level exposure documented only through the trespass arrest and the men's-ward hold.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crimes statute covers gender identity. Division civil-rights coverage removed, so state anti-discrimination recourse is absent.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims facing a hostile division enforcement posture may be less willing or able to rely on police.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state remedy for service, housing or employment refusal on gender identity; localities preempted from stronger protections. Enforcement of the school rule against adult visitors is not documented beyond the statute's wording.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment protection (2020 ruling) and national hate-crimes statute exist; federal litigation is ongoing and several orders are enjoined. Some civil-liberties litigation has operated.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Federal protections partly operate; division layer removes state recourse, and the state trespass and school rules remove discretion for visitors on public or school premises.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest analogue: birth-sex housing with assault exposure, a cross-dressing arrest statute for administrative buildings, and no execution. This case shares the facility-trespass arrest and birth-sex custody harm, and adds universal school-ground exposure and federal immigration-custody sexual abuse. It is roughly similar, perhaps slightly lower, because there is no state remedy and federal custody abuse is documented.

Visitor register with routine exclusion and no arrest. This case has documented passport refusal and entry-cable exclusion, similar in kind. It is lower because it adds criminal trespass, birth-sex custody placement, and documented custody abuse, which the 0.35-A case lacks.

Birth-sex ward placement with partial denial of care and a recourse route but no detention. This case is materially lower: it adds a criminal trespass arrest, universal school-ground restroom exposure for visitors, removal of state civil-rights recourse, and documented federal custody abuse.

Impersonation arrests with jail assault and blocked monitors. This case is higher: no capital provision is documented, the trespass offence requires a refusal step, and civil-liberties litigation has operated. The custody harm is nonetheless documented, which is why it is not higher still.

Working employment anti-discrimination with reinstatement and damages. This case is far lower: gender identity is removed from state civil-rights law and preempted locally, there is no state employment remedy, and documented custody and facility exposure are absent from the anchor. To reach 0.75 this jurisdiction would need restored state protections, enforced remedies, and removal of the school and trespass rules.

parsed.synthesis: Entry screening, passport markers, and a discrepancy-triggered fraud route set the federal gate. The division layer adds criminal trespass for facility refusal, a universal school-ground birth-certificate restroom rule, and no state remedy after removal of gender identity from civil-rights law. Documented custody harms (immigration abuse, birth-sex placement, and a 24-hour men's-ward hold) show how a document or facility incident can escalate into severe treatment. Care is blocked for minors and proposed federal rules add pressure. Mitigations are partial: national employment and hate-crime statutes exist, several federal orders are enjoined, and litigation continues. Violence risk is not quantified and is treated as undocumented. Overall the combined regime is materially restrictive and places the jurisdiction in the lower-elevated band, with no capital or systematic-imprisonment exposure documented.
